extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalists, and PR/communications practitioners
extracted.subtask_short: writing press releases for media pickup
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts criteria that make a press release likely to be used (or used verbatim) by newsrooms, based on Lewis et al.'s study of British journalism and the phenomenon of 'churnalism'. Useful for PR authors aiming to maximize pickup and for researchers evaluating press-release influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-formatted as news
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release presented in news form (e.g., AP-style, inverted pyramid) is more likely to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formatting the release like a news article reduces the need for newsroom re-writing and makes it plug-and-play for editors and sub-editors; use inverted-pyramid structure and standard news style conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contains all necessary attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include names, titles, and contact information so the item is fully attributed and usable as-is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing complete attribution and contact details removes a routine verification/lookup step for reporters and increases likelihood of direct use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has quotes ready to use
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide usable quotations in the release so journalists do not need to conduct interviews to include a quote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes should be well-crafted, concise, and newsworthy; pre-made quotes lower newsroom workload and encourage verbatim or lightly edited insertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Has visuals attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach images, video, or other visuals to reduce production work for publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing high-quality visuals (with captions/credits) increases pick-up by outlets that need ready-to-run imagery or multimedia assets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comes from a trusted source
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases originating from major institutions or trusted organisations are more likely to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms shortcut verification and prefer sources with established reputations; institutional provenance increases credibility and pickup probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distributed via wire services
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution through wire services (e.g., Reuters, AP, PA) amplifies reach and increases the chance of reuse by news outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wired distribution places the release in the pipelines journalists already monitor and can be copied directly into copy desks or feeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed properly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use embargoes that align with publication schedules to increase coordinated publication and pickup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, respected embargo dates/times allow newsrooms to schedule coverage and increases likelihood the material is used at the desired moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized (regional angle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a regional/local angle to make a release relevant to local/regional outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localization — geography, local statistics, named local spokespeople — makes a release more salient to regional desks and increases pick-up by local media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit Rubric for 'Churnalism-Ready' Press Release
rubrics_metrics.description: An aggregate checklist of attributes that make a release ready to be recycled as news (i.e., ‘churned’ into copy without original reporting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components noted by the study: length matching news expectations (e.g., 300–500 words for a brief; longer for features); headlines that function as news headlines; a lead that reads as a news lead; usable quotes; a background paragraph that provides standalone context; and author/source information prepared so the item can be given a byline. Designing a release to meet these elements increases chances of verbatim or lightly-edited reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release as 'ready-to-print' / 'pre-packaged news'
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases crafted to be plug-and-play reduce the need for original reporting and are therefore more likely to be run wholesale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper highlights newsroom resource constraints and production pressures (fewer reporters, higher output targets) that create demand for ready-to-print material; producers aiming for pickup should prioritize completeness and news-format packaging, while critics should be aware this practice (churnalism) can reduce democratic accountability.
